mainTopic: A raped wife and כהונה, lashes for a כהן whose wife was raped, and whether a forbidden engagement to a כהן stops a woman from eating תרומה.
overview: The amud opens with a ruling that an אשת ישראל who was raped stays permitted to her husband but becomes unfit for כהונה. It is supported from the word "וכן" in our משנה. The גמרא pushes the proof off by searching for another detail "וכן" might carry over, and it settles on שלא כדרכה with חייבי לאוין. Next comes a ruling that a כהן whose wife was raped is lashed for living with her. In one version this is רבא's ruling, giving lashes for זונה as well as טומאה. In the other version it is רבה's ruling, giving lashes for טומאה only. רבי זירא objects that the ban is only a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, which carries no lashes. The answer in each version is that every wife starts out under a real לאו, and the פסוק removes only the forced ישראל's wife. A new משנה then asks whether a woman forbidden to a כהן may eat תרומה while she is only engaged to him. The גמרא brings רבי מאיר's קל וחומר and the Sages' answer to it. Finally it applies this argument to a פצוע דכא כהן engaged to a בת ישראל, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A raped wife is still permitted to her husband but unfit for a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The אמורא rules that an אשת ישראל who was raped stays permitted to her husband but becomes פסולה לכהונה, and he says the משנה proves it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He opened our eyes from the משנה: the wife of a ישראל who was raped, even though she is still permitted to her husband, is unfit to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling about a married woman who was raped and says it can be shown from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being forced does not make her forbidden to her ישראל husband. Still, the act counts as forbidden relations, so she becomes a זונה for כהונה and may not marry a כהן later, for example after her husband dies.

keyTerms.meaning: He lit up our eyes, meaning he showed us a clear source
She was forced (raped)
Permitted to her husband
Unfit to marry a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two rules. Toward her own husband she stays permitted, because she was forced. Toward a כהן she is unfit, because the act itself is what matters for כהונה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that unfitness for כהונה depends on the act, not on whether the woman is to blame.

phrases.english: And he lit up our eyes from the משנה:
phrases.notes: He means he showed a clear source for his ruling in our own משנה.

phrases.english: The wife of a ישראל who was raped,
even though she is permitted to her husband,
she is unfit to marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this sugya.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשת ישראל who was raped is permitted to her husband but פסולה לכהונה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's "וכן" line
steps.stepSummary: The source is quoted: the משנה says "וכן" one who has relations with any of the עריות or פסולות disqualifies her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה also taught: And so too, one who has relations with any of the forbidden relations stated in the תורה, or with women unfit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: This step quotes the משנה line the proof will use. It is preparing the next move, where the גמרא explains what "וכן" means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this line, the משנה listed details about a יבם and his יבמה, including whether the act was forced or willing. The word "וכן" links this new case back to that list. Which details it carries over is what the rest of the sugya is about.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא taught, meaning the משנה itself says
And so too, a word that links back to the earlier case
Forbidden relations listed in the תורה
Women unfit to marry him, even though they are not עריות

phrases.english: And our תנא taught:
phrases.notes: "Our תנא" is the author of our own משנה.

phrases.english: And so too, one who has relations with one
of all the forbidden relations stated in the תורה,
or with women unfit for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה source promised in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a raped wife is unfit for כהונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's "וכן הבא על אחת מכל העריות" line.

steps.title: "וכן" includes a forced act, so rape disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The proof says "וכן" carries over the forced-or-willing detail, so even a forced act disqualifies her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "and so too" mean? Doesn't it mean there is no difference whether by mistake or on purpose, forced or willing, and the משנה teaches that he disqualified her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the משנה proves the ruling: "וכן" means all the earlier details apply here too, including being forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "וכן" carries over "באונס", then even a forced act with עריות disqualifies the woman. That is exactly the ruling about the raped wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that, a way of pushing a reading as the obvious one
There is no difference
By mistake / on purpose
Forced / willing
He disqualified her

phrases.english: What does "and so too" mean?
Doesn't it mean: no difference whether by mistake
or on purpose,
and no difference whether forced
or willing,
and it teaches: he disqualified her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the quoted משנה.
steps.raayaObject: A forced act still disqualifies the woman from כהונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: "וכן" read as carrying over the forced-or-willing detail from the יבמה case.

steps.title: Maybe "וכן" refers only to the first stage of relations
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: perhaps "וכן" carries over only the rule that העראה counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. "And so too" refers to the first stage of relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by suggesting "וכן" carries over a different detail from the earlier list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "וכן" means only that העראה also disqualifies, then the משנה says nothing about a forced act. The proof about the raped wife would be gone.

keyTerms.meaning: The first stage of relations, not completed

phrases.english: No. What does "and so too" mean? It refers to the first stage of relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 3's reading of "וכן".
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading that "וכן" includes a forced act.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: "וכן" could be pointing to העראה instead.

steps.title: העראה with עריות could not be learned from יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the העראה reading: the rule that העראה counts is written first about עריות, so עריות cannot be learned from יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first stage of relations with whom? If you say with עריות, are we learning עריות from a יבמה? Just the opposite: we learn יבמה from עריות, since the main source for העראה is written about עריות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection, saying "וכן" cannot mean העראה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "וכן" makes it sound as if the rule for עריות is borrowed from the יבמה case. But the תורה wrote the rule of העראה about עריות, and יבמה learns it from there. So the משנה would not present עריות as the follower.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
Is that to say?
We learn
Just the opposite
The main source

phrases.english: The first stage of relations with whom?
If you say with forbidden relations,
is that to say we learn forbidden relations from a יבמה?
phrases.notes: "וכן" sounds as if the עריות case is copying the יבמה case before it.

phrases.english: Just the opposite: we learn יבמה from forbidden relations,
since the main source for the first stage is written about forbidden relations!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the העראה reading from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that "וכן" refers to העראה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "וכן" would mean עריות learns from יבמה, but the source for העראה is written about עריות, so it is the other way around.

steps.title: Maybe "וכן" refers to unnatural relations
steps.stepSummary: A new suggestion: "וכן" carries over the rule that שלא כדרכה relations count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does "and so too" mean? It refers to unnatural relations with עריות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another way to read "וכן" that still avoids the proof about a forced act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier list also said that a יבם acquires with relations שלא כדרכה. Perhaps "וכן" only teaches that such relations with עריות also disqualify, which again says nothing about אונס.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
Unnatural relations

phrases.english: Rather, what does "and so too" mean?
It refers to unnatural relations with forbidden relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed העראה reading with a new one, still pushing off step 3's proof.

steps.title: Unnatural relations are also written first about עריות
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge returns: the source for שלא כדרכה, "משכבי אשה", is written about עריות, so עריות would not learn it from יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just the opposite: the main source for "the lyings of a woman" is written about עריות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the new suggestion with the same argument it used against העראה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that unnatural relations count comes from the words "משכבי אשה", written about עריות. So the משנה would not say "וכן" as if עריות learns it from יבמה. This brings the proof about a forced act back into play.

keyTerms.meaning: "The lyings of a woman", the source that unnatural relations count
It is written

steps.whatToRemember: "וכן" cannot mean העראה or שלא כדרכה with עריות, because the source for both is written about עריות. The next step gives a reading of "וכן" that avoids this problem.

phrases.english: Just the opposite: the main source for "the lyings of a woman"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:22

phrases.english: is written about forbidden relations!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 6 using the same reasoning as step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that "וכן" refers to שלא כדרכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source for שלא כדרכה is written about עריות, so עריות would not be presented as learning it from יבמה.

steps.title: "וכן" refers to unusual relations with women forbidden by a plain לאו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on a reading of "וכן" that survives the challenge: it carries over the rule of שלא כדרכה for חייבי לאוין, where "משכבי אשה" is not written.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does "and so too" refer to? To unusual relations with women forbidden by an ordinary prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question of what "וכן" adds. It points to women forbidden only by a לאו, not by כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 7 was that עריות already have their own פסוק, "משכבי אשה", so they cannot learn from יבמה. חייבי לאוין are not עריות, and that פסוק is not written about them. So they really can learn the שלא כדרכה rule from יבמה. Since "וכן" now has a real job that has nothing to do with being forced, רב ששת's proof from it falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Women forbidden by an ordinary prohibition, which is punished with lashes, not כרת
Unusual (non-standard) relations
Rather (introduces a new answer after the earlier ones failed)

steps.whatToRemember: "וכן" teaches that שלא כדרכה counts for חייבי לאוין, as it does for a יבמה. So it does not prove that a forced act disqualifies her, and רב ששת's proof is not conclusive.

phrases.english: Rather, what is "and so too"?
It refers to unusual relations by those forbidden by a prohibition.
phrases.notes: These are women forbidden by a plain לאו, where the phrase "משכבי אשה" is not written, so they can learn from יבמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7 by moving the meaning of "וכן" from עריות to חייבי לאוין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the scope of the word "וכן"
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "וכן" was thought to carry over a rule that עריות already have from their own פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: "וכן" carries over the שלא כדרכה rule to חייבי לאוין, who have no separate פסוק for it.

steps.title: רבא: a כהן is lashed for living with his wife after she was forced
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if a כהן's wife was forced, her husband gets lashes for being with her, because she has the status of a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wife of a priest who was forced — her husband is lashed on her account because of the prohibition of a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רבא teaches that a forced כהן's wife is forbidden to him, and that he gets מלקות because of the איסור of זונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary Jewish woman who was forced stays permitted to her husband, but a כהן's wife does not. רבא names the specific prohibition the husband breaks: a כהן may not be with a זונה. That is a לאו, so it carries lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of a כהן
Who was forced (did not consent)
Gets lashes (מלקות)
A woman who had forbidden relations, forbidden to a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the subject of the rest of this section. Its wording and its source are both challenged next.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The wife of a priest who was forced,
her husband is lashed on her account because of zona.
phrases.notes: He means: if the husband goes on living with her after this happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement on a related theme: a forced wife who becomes forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who is with his wife after she was forced gets מלקות because of the איסור of זונה.

steps.title: Why only זונה and not also טומאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that רבא mentions only זונה, since the תורה also calls such a wife "טמאה" and forbids her to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of זונה, yes; because of טומאה, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of רבא's ruling. It asks why he lists only זונה and leaves out the איסור of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls a married woman who was with another man "טמאה" to her husband, and that is also a prohibition. רבא's words "because of זונה" sound like there is only one reason for lashes. The גמרא asks why טומאה is not a reason as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The status of a wife who was with another man, which forbids her to her husband
Yes

phrases.english: Because of zona, yes,
because of impurity, no?
phrases.notes: The תורה calls such a wife "טמאה" to her husband, so the גמרא expects this reason to apply too.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם זוֹנָה אִין, מִשּׁוּם טוּמְאָה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבא's ruling from Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming only זונה suggests that טומאה gives no lashes, yet the תורה forbids such a wife because of טומאה as well.

steps.title: Read רבא as saying "also because of זונה"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adjusts רבא's words: the husband is lashed for טומאה and also for זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: also because of זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adjusting רבא's wording. He meant that the husband gets lashes for זונה in addition to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה is obvious, so רבא did not need to mention it. His new point is that the זונה prohibition applies here too. So the husband breaks two prohibitions, not one.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read it this way instead)
Also, even

phrases.english: Say: also because of zona.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adjusting the wording of the statement ("say also")
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא gave זונה as the only reason for lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא meant lashes for זונה in addition to טומאה.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the ban on a forced כהן's wife is only a לאו הבא מכלל עשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes a ברייתא showing that the ban on a forced כהן's wife is learned indirectly. A prohibition learned that way counts as an עשה, so there should be no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: "And she was not taken" — then she is forbidden; but if she was taken by force, she is permitted. And you have another woman who is forbidden even though she was taken by force. Which is she? The wife of a priest. And a prohibition that comes from a positive command is a positive command!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges רבא's ruling that the husband gets lashes. He cites a ברייתא about the source of the ban on a forced כהן's wife, then states why that source rules out lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק as saying that a forced wife is permitted, and it learns from an extra word that a כהן's wife is forbidden even when forced. That ban is never stated directly. It is inferred from what is permitted to others, which makes it a לאו הבא מכלל עשה. Such a prohibition has the weight of an עשה, and there are no מלקות for an עשה, so רבא's ruling seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source
Was seized (taken by force)
A prohibition that is not stated, only inferred from a positive statement
A positive command; no lashes for breaking it

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא agrees with רבא that a forced כהן's wife is forbidden. רבי זירא is not arguing about whether she is forbidden. He is arguing only about whether the husband gets lashes for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move: the גמרא must explain how רבא can give lashes when the source seems to be only a לאו הבא מכלל עשה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objected:
"And she was not taken" — she is forbidden,
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13

phrases.english: but if she was taken by force, she is permitted.
And you have another woman
phrases.notes: This is learned from the extra word "וְהִיא", "and she", in the פסוק.

phrases.english: who, even though she was taken by force, is forbidden,
and which is she? This is the wife of a priest.
And a prohibition that comes from a positive statement is a positive command!
phrases.notes: So no lashes should be given, since lashes are only for breaking a real לאו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lashes in רבא's ruling, as clarified in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the husband of a forced כהן's wife gets lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ban on a forced כהן's wife comes only from an inference (a לאו הבא מכלל עשה), which has the weight of an עשה. There are no lashes for an עשה.

steps.title: רבה: every adulterous wife starts out as a זונה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers רבי זירא: every wife who was with another man starts out as a זונה. The תורה took out only a forced ישראל's wife, so a forced כהן's wife stays a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: All such women were included in the category of זונה. The verse took out only the wife of a ישראל: 'and she was not taken' means she is forbidden, so if she was taken by force, she is permitted. This shows that the wife of a כהן stays as she was, still a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge from step 12, which said the ban on a forced כהן's wife is only an עשה and should bring no lashes. He shows that her ban is really the לאו of זונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא thought the ban on a forced כהן's wife came only indirectly from the words 'והיא לא נתפשה'. רבה turns this around. The basic rule is that every such wife is a זונה, and the verse only removes the forced ישראל's wife from that rule. Nothing removes the כהן's wife, so she stays a זונה, and that is a real לאו with lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: included in a category
a woman forbidden to a כהן because of a forbidden relationship
specified, took out one case from a general rule
she was taken (by force)
she stays as she was

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer changes the source of the ban. It is not a weak indirect rule. It comes from the general category of זונה, and that category carries lashes.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
All were included in the category of zonah,
phrases.notes: "All" means every married woman who was with another man, whether willingly or by force.

phrases.english: when the verse specified for you
regarding the wife of a Yisrael

phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13

phrases.english: so if she was taken, she is permitted
this implies that the wife of a kohen

phrases.notes: He means she stays in the זונה category even though she was forced.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the source: the general rule includes everyone, and the verse removes only one case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on a forced כהן's wife comes only indirectly from 'והיא', so it counts as an עשה
steps.terutzMaskana: She stays in the general category of זונה, which is a לאו, so the husband is lashed

steps.title: Second version: רבה gives lashes only for impurity
steps.stepSummary: A second version of רבה's ruling: the husband of a forced כהן's wife is lashed because of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say a different version. רבה said: When a כהן's wife was raped, her husband is lashed for being with her because of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רבה's statement. In this version the lashes come only because she is 'טמאה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the statement was רבא's. After the wording was adjusted in step 11, it gave lashes for זונה in addition to טומאה. In this version רבה names only טומאה, and the גמרא is about to read something into what he left out.

steps.title: Inference: a forced woman is not called a זונה
steps.stepSummary: Since רבה mentioned only טומאה, the גמרא infers that a forced woman is not considered a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of טומאה, yes; because of זונה, no. So in a case of force, she is not called a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from what רבה left out: forcing does not make a woman a זונה. This sets up רבי זירא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If force made her a זונה, רבה would have said so. In this version, the only basis for lashes is טומאה. So the next question becomes whether טומאה here is a real לאו.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the second version, force does not make a woman a זונה; only טומאה applies

steps.title: רבי זירא: the impurity ban is only an indirect rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges: the ban on a forced כהן's wife comes from 'והיא', which is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, and that counts as an עשה with no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: 'And she was not taken' means she is forbidden, so if she was taken, she is permitted. And you have another woman who is forbidden even though she was taken. Which one? The wife of a כהן. But a prohibition that comes out of a positive statement counts as a positive commandment!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks the second version. If the ban on a forced כהן's wife comes only indirectly, there should be no lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes are given only for breaking a real לאו. The ban here is learned by implication from the extra word 'והיא', and such a rule has only the strength of an עשה. So רבה's lashes for טומאה seem to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection from a source
a prohibition learned by implication from a positive statement
forbidden / permitted

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objected:
"and she was not taken": she is forbidden,
so if she was taken, she is permitted.
And you have another woman,
phrases.notes: This 'other woman' is learned from the extra word 'והיא', 'and she'.

phrases.english: who, even though she was taken, is forbidden,
and which is she? This is the wife of a kohen,
and a prohibition that comes out of a positive statement
is a positive commandment!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version (lashes for טומאה)
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling in the second version that the husband is lashed for טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ban is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה, which counts as an עשה, so no lashes can be given

steps.title: רבא: every wife starts out under 'after she was made impure'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: every wife starts out included in the לאו of 'אחרי אשר הוטמאה'. The תורה took out only a forced ישראל's wife, so a forced כהן's wife stays under that לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: All were included in 'after she was made impure'. When the verse specified about a ישראל's wife that 'she was not taken' means she is forbidden, so if she was taken she is permitted, this shows that a כהן's wife stays as she was, still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the lashes for טומאה. They come from a real לאו, not from an indirect rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same method רבה used in step 13, now applied to טומאה. 'אחרי אשר הוטמאה' is a לאו, and it starts out covering every such wife. Only the forced ישראל's wife is removed from it, so the forced כהן's wife is still under the לאו and her husband is lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: she was made impure (from the verse about remarrying a divorced wife)
by implication, it follows that
the verse

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions use the same method: a general category covers every wife, and the verse 'והיא לא נתפשה' removes only the forced ישראל's wife. In the first version that category is זונה; in the second it is the לאו of 'אחרי אשר הוטמאה'. Either way, the forced כהן's wife stays under a real לאו, so there are lashes.

phrases.english: Rava said:
All were included in
"after she was made impure,"
phrases.notes: דברים 24:4

phrases.english: when the verse specified for you
regarding the wife of a Yisrael
"and she was not taken": she is forbidden,
so if she was taken, she is permitted,
this implies that the wife of a kohen
remains as she was.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַכֹּל הָיוּ בִּכְלַל ״אַחֲרֵי אֲשֶׁר הֻטַּמָּאָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge to the second version
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the source: the לאו of 'הוטמאה' covers everyone, and the verse removes only one case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טומאה ban on a forced כהן's wife is only a לאו הבא מכלל עשה
steps.terutzMaskana: She stays under the explicit לאו of 'אחרי אשר הוטמאה', so the husband is lashed

steps.title: A forbidden engagement to a כהן and eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a woman who is forbidden to a כהן and only engaged to him may not eat תרומה. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון disagree and allow her to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a widow is engaged to a כהן גדול, or a divorcée or חלוצה is engaged to a regular כהן, she may not eat תרומה just from the engagement. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say she may.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It asks whether an engagement that the תורה forbids already stops a woman from eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these women is forbidden to the כהן she got engaged to. The first opinion says the forbidden engagement by itself takes away her right to eat תרומה. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say the engagement alone does not do this.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat
The first stage of marriage (engagement); the couple do not live together yet
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
A widow released from יבום through חליצה; she is forbidden to a כהן
They declare her fit (allowed to eat)

steps.confusionAlert: Each case pairs a woman with the כהן she is forbidden to: a widow is forbidden only to a כהן גדול, while a divorcée and a חלוצה are forbidden even to a regular כהן.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A widow engaged to a High Priest,
a divorcée or a חלוצה engaged to a regular priest,
from the engagement alone,
they may not eat תרומה.
רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון declare them fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First opinion: a forbidden engagement to a כהן already stops her from eating תרומה. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון: she may still eat.

steps.title: After being widowed or divorced: marriage versus engagement
steps.stepSummary: If these women were widowed or divorced after full marriage, they are disqualified. If it happened during the engagement stage, they are fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they became widowed or divorced after full marriage, they are disqualified. If it was only after engagement, they are fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and asks what happens once the forbidden relationship has ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After full marriage, the forbidden living together leaves a lasting mark, so she stays disqualified. If they were only engaged, nothing lasting happened, so she goes back to being fit, and even the first opinion agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Full marriage, the stage when the couple live together
Disqualified
Fit, allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the first opinion's ban during engagement is only temporary. Only full marriage causes lasting damage.

phrases.english: If they were widowed or divorced,
from full marriage, they are disqualified;
from engagement, they are fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the case where the forbidden relationship has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ended after full marriage: disqualified. Ended after engagement only: fit.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's קל וחומר for the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's proof. Even a permitted engagement can stop a woman from eating תרומה, so a sinful engagement should surely stop her too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי מאיר said: this is a קל וחומר. A permitted engagement already stops her from eating תרומה, so a sinful engagement should do so all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר gives a reason for the first opinion of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A permitted engagement, such as a כהן's daughter engaged to a regular ישראל, ends her right to eat תרומה. רבי מאיר reasons that if an allowed engagement has this power, a sinful engagement should have it even more.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A logical argument from a lighter case to a heavier case
A permitted engagement
An engagement that breaks a prohibition

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught in a ברייתא:
רבי מאיר said: this is a קל וחומר.
If a permitted engagement does not let her eat,
phrases.notes: Think of a כהן's daughter engaged to a regular ישראל. That engagement ends her right to eat her father's תרומה.

phrases.english: then surely a sinful engagement does not!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a logical source for the first opinion in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The first opinion that a forbidden engagement already stops her from eating תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from a permitted engagement, which already stops her from eating.

steps.title: חכמים break the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: חכמים answer that a regular ישראל can never give a woman the right to eat תרומה, but a כהן can in other cases. So the comparison does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: No. A permitted engagement to a ישראל is different, because a ישראל can never give her תרומה to eat. A sinful engagement to a כהן is different, because a כהן can give her תרומה to eat in other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים reject רבי מאיר's קל וחומר by showing that the 'lighter' case has its own reason to be strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Engagement to a ישראל takes away תרומה because a ישראל never has the power to feed תרומה. A כהן does have that power when the marriage is permitted, so his engagement does not automatically take it away, even when it is forbidden. Because of this difference, the קל וחומר breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the other Sages) said to him
To give her the right to eat (תרומה)
Another case or situation

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר argued with a קל וחומר: a permitted engagement already stops her from eating תרומה, so a sinful one surely does. חכמים answered that a ישראל can never give תרומה, but a כהן can, so the cases are not alike.

phrases.english: They said to him: No.
If you say this about a permitted engagement,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵין לוֹ לְהַאֲכִיל בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.english: that is because he cannot give her the right to eat in any other case,
phrases.notes: A regular ישראל can never give his wife תרומה to eat, in any situation.

phrases.english: will you say the same about a sinful engagement,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹ לְהַאֲכִיל בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
phrases.english: where he can give her the right to eat in another case?
phrases.notes: A כהן can give his wife תרומה when he marries a woman he is allowed to marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי מאיר's קל וחומר as a proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'lighter' case is strict for its own reason: a ישראל never has the power to feed תרומה, but a כהן does.

steps.title: A new case that fits the earlier argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says in the name of רבי אושעיא that a כהן who is a פצוע דכא and became engaged to a בת ישראל depends on the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: if a כהן with a crushed or damaged reproductive organ became engaged to a regular Jewish woman, we have reached the argument between רבי מאיר on one side and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון on the other.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא brings a new case and says it depends on the argument we just learned about engaged women who are forbidden to their husbands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids a פצוע דכא to marry a regular Jewish woman, so this engagement is a forbidden one. That makes it just like the women in the earlier argument: engaged to a כהן, but forbidden to live with him. So whether she may eat תרומה depends on which side of that argument we follow.

keyTerms.meaning: A man whose reproductive organ is crushed or damaged. The תורה forbids him to marry a regular Jewish woman.
Made a formal engagement (קידושין), the first stage of Jewish marriage
A Jewish woman who is not from a כהן's family
We have reached the argument. This case depends on an argument we already know.

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי אלעזר who reports this statement is a later teacher (an אמורא). He is not the same person as the רבי אלעזר in the argument, who is a תנא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the earlier argument is not only about the women listed in the משנה. It reaches any engagement that the תורה forbids, including this one.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
A priest with crushed testicles
phrases.notes: The rule that such a man may not marry into the Jewish people comes from דברים 23:2.

phrases.english: who betrothed the daughter of an Israelite,
we have arrived at the dispute

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: of Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: This is the argument from steps 18 and 20: may a woman forbidden to her כהן eat תרומה while she is only engaged?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the argument from steps 18 to 21 and applies it to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פצוע דכא כהן who became engaged to a בת ישראל falls under the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.

steps.title: According to רבי מאיר she may not eat
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a woman waiting for a relationship the תורה forbids may not eat תרומה, so this woman may not eat either.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי מאיר, who said that a woman waiting for a relationship forbidden by the תורה may not eat תרומה, this woman also may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי מאיר's side of the argument applies to the case of the פצוע דכא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says that even being engaged for a forbidden relationship blocks the woman from eating תרומה. Her future relationship with a פצוע דכא is forbidden by the תורה. So by his view she cannot eat תרומה, even during the engagement.

keyTerms.meaning: Waiting for, or set aside for. Here it describes an engaged woman who is waiting to live with her husband.
A forbidden relationship between husband and wife
From the תורה itself, not a rabbinic rule
She eats. Here it means she may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir, who said
that a woman reserved for intercourse that is prohibited by Torah law
may not partake of teruma —
this one may also not partake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the argument mentioned in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a בת ישראל engaged to a פצוע דכא כהן may not eat תרומה.

steps.title: Starting the view of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the other side: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold that a woman waiting for a forbidden relationship may eat תרומה. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, who say that a woman waiting for a relationship forbidden by the תורה may eat תרומה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the other side of the argument. The sentence is not finished here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון let a forbidden engaged woman eat תרומה until the forbidden relationship actually happens. One might expect that they would simply let this woman eat as well. But the גמרא has not finished its sentence yet, so the next amud shows how it applies to the פצוע דכא.

keyTerms.meaning: Who say. This form is used when two or more people say something together.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the answer yet. The sentence is cut off, and the גמרא may point out something special about the פצוע דכא case.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, who say
that a woman reserved for intercourse that is prohibited by Torah law
may partake of teruma —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי מאיר's side to the other side of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold that a woman waiting for a forbidden relationship may eat תרומה. How this applies to the פצוע דכא comes on the next amud.
